title: Polynomial Sums for Moduli with Prime-Power Divisors
summary: Squarefree moduli admit an exact formula and generally nonzero sums; for moduli with prime-power divisors, exact characterization and useful zero-sum behavior remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a polynomial function $F$ over $\mathbb{Z}_q$, where $q$ has prime-power divisors, determine an exact characterization of the sum $\sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}_q} F(x) \bmod q$ and establish whether this sum can satisfy a useful zero-sum property. The corresponding behavior for such moduli is unresolved; in particular, small-scale experiments over $\mathbb{Z}_{2^y}$ suggest that the sum is not zero.

scope.domain: Algebraic behavior of polynomial sums over residue rings in symmetric cryptanalysis.
assumptions: F is a polynomial function over the residue ring modulo q.
parameters: F: polynomial function whose values are summed
q: modulus defining the residue ring and reduction of the sum
y: exponent in the power-of-two rings used in small-scale experiments
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the sum modulo q for moduli with prime-power divisors and determine whether it can satisfy a useful zero-sum property.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Symmetric Primitives over Rings and a Key Recovery Attack on Rubato

progress.summary: The source contrasts the exact squarefree-modulus formula with the missing characterization when q has prime-power divisors. Small power-of-two experiments suggest that the sum is nonzero rather than yielding a zero-sum.
citation_labels: Lorenzo Grassi et al., Cryptanalysis of Symmetric Primitives over Rings and a Key Recovery Attack on Rubato
